title: Prompt anchor merging and sparse-KV compression for inter-request sharing
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Our current per-request prefix/KV caching duplicates similar prompt prefixes across tenants and sessions, bloating GPU resident memory and increasing eviction churn under high-concurrency microbatching. This ticket prototypes a runtime component that (1) identifies stable 'prompt anchors' (canonicalized prefix kernels) across requests, (2) merges equivalent anchors into a shared, content-addressed KV entry, and (3) stores a sparse compressed representation for merged anchors to reduce GPU memory while preserving fast rehydration into the GPU KV cache for continuous batching.

Goals:
- Reduce duplicate KV blobs stored in GPU memory for common prompt fragments by >= 40% in multi-tenant workloads.
- Maintain tail latency SLOs (p99 latency increase < 5ms) for cold/hit paths.
- Integrate with continuous batching so that anchor matches are applied before microbatch formation, allowing batch-level reuse.

Constraints:
- Must be compatible with existing KV encoding (chunked key/value shards) and not require model changes.
- Solution should support tenant isolation: shared anchors are allowed only when policy permits (tenant opt-in and size thresholds).
- GPU residency bookkeeping must remain lock-free on the hot path; any heavier work should be offloaded to background compaction threads.

Why this is different: Instead of aggressively deduplicating raw prompt strings, we introduce an intermediate 'anchor' abstraction (normalized, slot-annotated fragment) that tolerates small tokenization differences and focuses dedupe on model-meaningful fragments. We also use a sparse delta compression format for merged anchor entries to keep GPU-resident footprint low and accelerate rehydration via patch-based merge when a batch requests a variant.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrated into serving runtime and can be toggled via runtime flag
End-to-end e2e test that simulates 1k concurrent microbatches and shows >=40% reduction in unique GPU-resident KV entries for a synthetic multi-tenant prompt corpus
p99 token-generation latency degradation <= 5ms on 8xA100 runs compared to baseline without anchor dedupe
Cost telemetry shows >=20% token-cost improvement for mixed chat/slot workloads in internal replay tests
Security policy gating implemented: tenant-level allowlist and audit logging for anchor sharing operations
design_notes: Anchor extraction: tokenize first N tokens of input prompt and apply deterministic normalization (whitespace collapse, slot placeholder mapping, header strip). Produce anchor fingerprint (64-bit rolling hash + sim-hash vector for fuzzy matching).
Matching strategy: two-stage -- exact fingerprint match (fast path) then HNSW ANN on a compact embedding of anchor tokens for fuzzy merge with similarity threshold T (configurable, default 0.92).

Storage layout: content-addressed anchor store with entries: {anchor_id, canonical_token_span, sparse_delta_blob, refcount}. In practice we store canonical_token_span as metadata off-GPU and only sparse_delta_blob on-GPU when needed.

Sparse compression: run-length + delta-encoding across token embeddings and KV deltas; fallback to full blob if compression ratio > R. Implement GPU copy-friendly slab format (aligned chunks) to avoid extra memcpy.

GPU residency model: maintain lightweight shard header on-GPU pointing to slab; background compactor merges small slabs into coalesced pages during low-load windows. Hot-path access uses header lookup + inlined patch apply kernel that reconstructs requested KV entries in-place without async roundtrips to CPU when possible.

Eviction policy: refcount + hotness score; merged anchors have a 'merge_entropy' metric to prefer keeping high-reuse canonical anchors. Eviction triggers background delta-spill to CPU cache with fast rehydrate path.
Multi-tenant isolation: anchors carry tenant bitmask and ACL. We only permit cross-tenant sharing when tenant owner sets allowShare=true; otherwise we maintain per-tenant canonicalization caches.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy feature toggled off by default in runtime-1.20 to two internal clusters; enable for internal test tenants only
Phase 2 (internal traffic): enable for replayed multi-tenant logs and run nightly compact/rehydration benchmarks; collect refcounts and eviction delta metrics
Phase 3 (customer opt-in): expose policy flag in Console for customers to opt-in to anchor sharing and monitor for regressions
Phase 4 (default-on for low-risk workloads): enable by default for single-tenant Dedicated pools where SLA and security constraints allow
benchmarks: Baseline (no anchor dedupe): unique GPU-resident KV entries: 184K for 30M prompt fragments replay
Prototype (early implementation) on 8xA100: unique entries: 106K (42% reduction), average eviction rate down 31%
p50 token latency change: +0.2ms, p99: +3.8ms (meets p99 target <5ms) for synthetic mixed-chat workload
Cost proxy: token GPU-seconds decreased by 18% in replay runs using microbatch-aware anchor prefetching
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: fuzzy matching incorrectly merges semantically-distinct prefixes. Mitigation: conservative default threshold and rollback flag; run confusion detection job comparing model logits on merged vs original prefix during canaries.
Risk: background compaction impacts host CPU. Mitigation: compaction rate limiter and priority cgroups; evict-to-CPU path must be robust.

Risk: tenant privacy concerns with shared anchors. Mitigation: tenant allowlist, audit logs, and opt-in policy surfaced in Console; all shared anchor metadata is scrubbed of PII by normalization step.
Risk: added complexity on hot path increases latency. Mitigation: keep hot-path to fingerprint lookup + header probe; defer expensive ANN lookups to pre-batch scheduler thread pool.
